answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat trust like a grove that grows slowly: a new identity enters only through a narrow inlet, starting with tiny limits and earning larger rights by completing verifiable work that peers can check. Good behaviour builds a haven of reputation that cannot be copied in bulk, because each history is tied to distinct, costly effort and endorsements from long-standing agents who lose standing if they vouch for fakes. Mass copies stay shallow-rooted and capped.
